conventions.convention: The ground ring is a field k; all tensor products are algebraic over k, and Sweedler notation denotes finite tensor sums rather than individually specified components.
The right-right compatibility is ρ(mh)=Σ m₀h₁ ⊗ m₁h₂; coinvariants satisfy ρ(n)=n⊗1_H. Morphisms preserve both action and coaction.
A Hopf antipode satisfies both convolution-inverse equations; compositional bijectivity is not assumed.
The free Hopf module V⊗H has action (v⊗h)g=v⊗hg and coaction ρ(v⊗h)=Σ(v⊗h₁)⊗h₂.

load_bearing.statement: A right-right Hopf module is a right H-module and right H-comodule satisfying ρ(mh)=Σ m₀h₁⊗m₁h₂. Its coinvariants are {m∈M:ρ(m)=m⊗1_H}; morphisms preserve both structures.
For a right-right Hopf module M over a Hopf algebra H over a field k, P(m)=Σ m₀S(m₁) is linear with image in M^{coH}, fixes every coinvariant, and satisfies P²=P. No bijectivity of S is assumed.

For a Hopf algebra H over a field k and a right-right Hopf module M, α:M^{coH}⊗H→M, n⊗h↦nh, is an isomorphism of right-right Hopf modules with inverse β(m)=Σ P(m₀)⊗m₁. No bijectivity assumption on S is used.

For a field k, a Hopf algebra H over k, and any k-vector space V, the action (v⊗h)g=v⊗hg and coaction ρ(v⊗h)=Σ(v⊗h₁)⊗h₂ make V⊗H a right-right Hopf module. No finite-dimensionality or choice of basis for V is needed.
For any k-vector space V and Hopf algebra H over k, (V⊗H)^{coH}={v⊗1_H:v∈V}; v↦v⊗1_H is an isomorphism with inverse the restriction of id_V⊗ε.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.2 writes '(id_V⊗ε)ρ(v⊗h)=v⊗h'. Here ρ has target (V⊗H)⊗H, so the counit contraction requires id_{V⊗H}⊗ε, equivalently id_V⊗id_H⊗ε under reassociation. The displayed map omits the identity on the first H factor. The intended counitality calculation is immediate and the statement is sound.

seams_checked.note: The imported definition has coaction M→M⊗H, the same coassociativity and counit equations, and the same morphism equation. No AC-dependent kernel or rational-duality theorem is imported.

The bialgebra, antipode, anti-multiplication, and anti-comultiplication interfaces match their uses. The projection contracts the factors in the correct order; neither its proof nor the fundamental theorem assumes S is bijective.

This is contextual page precedence. The supplier treats left-module tensor products and finite duals; the assigned page defines its right-right category locally and does not import a duality or S-inverse assertion.

The dual-regular construction uses the exact right-right compatibility definition. The integral theorem F3 and Proof 1.1–2.1 use the action-map isomorphism without assuming antipode bijectivity. The Frobenius theorem F5 and Proof 1.1 specialize that isomorphism to the separately constructed dual-regular Hopf module and its identified coinvariants.
